coverageSpotVerification.detail: scripts/acceptance.mjs maps suite-required assertions to tests that do not exercise their observables. Tautological `assert(true)` tests: m2-a12, m2-a13, m2-a18, m3-a11, m4-a06, m4-a07, m5-a05, m6-a09, m6-a10, m6-a11, m8-a06; m2-a17 ends in assert(true) after computing nothing. Mismatched observables: m2-a22/a23/a24 read one page and never scroll or use a cursor; m3-a10 runs an in-chat search instead of checking a quote; m5-a10 and m8-a05 only check Array.isArray; m8-a01 checks typeof on the query, not the screen. A dishonest mapping was found in every milestone except M1, so M2 (execution-green) is adjudicated capability-failure, and M3, M4, M5, M6, and M8 (already non-green at execution) are likewise marked. M1's mappings are weak but honest: m1-a02/a03/a11 check backend state (profile exists, E_CONSTRAINT, asset URL) rather than visible UI, yet the mapped test does exercise the assertion's backend observable. All 58 suite tests passed on the grader's clean checkout (suiteResult pass). Divergence between suite and independent results: m2-a12, a20, a22, a23, a24; m4-a07; m5-a04, a05, a10; m6-a11; m8-a01, a03, a04, a05, a06, a07.

The Trending tab crashes (uncaught TypeError in Avatar via FeedCard): app/feed.tsx renders TrendingRow with children instead of the required `post` props.

defects.summary: Signing up with an email whose derived handle is taken creates the account and then fails profile creation. The user is left with a registered, profile-less account; retrying sign-up reports the email as already registered.
updateConversation always writes `background` from its argument, so changing the accent, disappearing setting, or title without re-sending the background silently deletes the chat background.

Digest counts are not scoped to the period: unreadMessages/unreadChats read the lifetime membership counters. Stale unread messages trigger a digest every period, and deleted or expired messages are never subtracted.
Reactions cannot be removed from the app: tapping the same emoji re-sends it and the server keeps it, since only an intent with emoji 'none' clears (and the UI never sends one).
View-once photos never render in the web app (the bubble only reads msg.photo), and web video messages carry no poster or playable media.
defects.evidence: trace.md#T2; src/ConversationThread.tsx Bubble mediaUri={photo ?? poster}; sendMedia poster null

defects.summary: Connected clients keep expired disappearing messages on screen: the thread merge keeps previously polled rows that the server no longer returns, so purge happens only on relaunch.

Feed like/repost/reply counts come from client-side lengths of capped edge queries (likesOf first 200, repostsOf first 200, repliesOf last 80), fetched by polling likesOf every 250 ms per visible item. Counts are wrong past the caps, and request load grows with every rendered item.

Trending ranks only the newest 200 top-level posts in the trailing 24 h (`posts[at >= since] last 200`). At envelope volume (50k posts replayed within a day), heavily-liked posts outside that slice are silently excluded.
Feeds never paginate in the app (first 20 rows only), and the thread screen lists replies newest-first.
The conversation screen sorts messages newest-first (newest bubble at the top) while auto-scrolling to the end of the list.
The custom-client demo does not page history or actually receive a message, and API.md omits the inbox row shape, history ordering, and cursor (`next`) semantics.
DM uniqueness is not enforced server-side: a client-supplied pairKey lets a second DM channel be created for an existing pair, which also shadows the original in handle-based routing.
Post validation is incomplete: kind 'images' is accepted with zero images and together with a video clip (the brief forbids mixing).
Non-admin group members can change a group's disappearing-messages setting (the brief restricts this to admins in groups).
Insights totals drift: un-reposting never decrements repostsReceived, and unliking never decrements the day's likesReceived bucket.
The seed is not re-runnable: a second run of the starter-m3 segment aborts with E_CONSTRAINT on group-create (no duplicates are written).

The scale-replay adapter drops the log's `# checkpoint` markers as comments, so replay never pauses at 10%/50%. The lane's verification covered only four named fixtures (not corpus counts or the busy-group roster).

The per-milestone iOS Hermes exports (dist/ios-hermes-m1…m8) are byte-identical copies of a single bundle built before later milestone code changed, so they are not per-milestone platform-proof builds.
defects.evidence: trace.md#T2 (identical entry-1d206c4a….hbc, 3161955 bytes, in every dist/ios-hermes-m*)

defects.summary: Web clients poll aggressively regardless of live queries: DeliverySync queries inbox plus per-conversation receipts every 400 ms, and the open thread polls messages every 400 ms and typing every 300 ms.
The duplicate-email sign-up error shows a raw backend code ('E_AUTH: that email already has an account; sign in instead').
Fixture persona passwords are hard-coded in lane test tooling (scripts/acceptance.mjs; the custom-client-demo default).

Independent execution shows much more of the product works at the backend and UI level: 71 of the 119 results pass (M2 22/27, M3 14/15, M4 8/12, M5 6/12, M6 5/13, M8 3/18). This quality evidence places O1 near the top of the sub-30 band rather than near zero, but it cannot lift uncredited milestones. No platform-proof native artifacts exist for M6/M8. See assertionResults and trace.md#T6.

O2.anchorsCited: Below the ~30 anchor ('multiple high-severity defects in core flows'); nowhere near ~60 ('a few medium defects off the happy path').
O2.justification: Beyond-checklist findings: 2 blockers (the Insights screen and the Trending tab crash, d-01/d-02) and 13 majors in core flows. The majors include offline sends crashing into an error overlay (d-03), silent loss of identical-text messages (d-04), unreliable live delivery (d-05), profile edits overwritten by a form race (d-06), orphaned accounts after a handle collision (d-07), background wiped by any chat-setting change (d-08), non-period digest counts (d-09), no reaction removal (d-10), view-once and video media not rendering (d-11), expired messages persisting on connected clients (d-12), client-derived capped counts with 250 ms polling (d-13), a Trending slice cap (d-14), and no feed pagination (d-15). There are also 10 minors and 2 cosmetics. Evidence pointers are in defects[].
